subject: Urgent: morning inference errors and latency spikes impacting customers (AstraTune)
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@astratune.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Cc: devops@astratune.com
Date: Sun, 4 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: URGENT: morning inference errors and latency spikes affecting customers

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a big spike in 500s and token-level latency at our 08:00 PST morning batch window this morning. ~40% of requests returned 500s for ~20 minutes and median generation latency jumped from ~150ms to >1.2s. This is impacting live customers and churn risk is real.

Attached are sample logs and a short timeline. We're running with your hosted API (model: redwood-v2-13b-quant) and have standard prefix caching enabled. Not sure if recent traffic changes on our end (batch surge) exposed something in your cache/batching layer, but the timing aligns with our peak.

We need immediate mitigation (routing, fallback to stable model variant, or temporary capacity bump) and an escalation to engineering/executive level. Please confirm receipt and ETA for first updates.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Head of Platform, AstraTune
ellen.park@astratune.com

Team — plumbing notes from the first pass:
- Customer: AstraTune (heavy morning batch window, concurrent prefix-heavy queries).
- Symptoms: 40% 500s for ~20m, median latency jump to >1.2s, backlog on hot lanes observed.
- Preliminary hypothesis: KV prefix cache thrash + HOL (head-of-line) blocking in the hot lane. Their traffic shows many large-batch requests that likely evict hot prefixes between windows, causing frequent KV miss storms and blocking lanes. Continuous batching + large max_batch_size likely increasing HOL-style queueing when prefixes miss.

Immediate asks:
1) Jonas — can you snapshot current hot-lane queue lengths and eviction rates for AstraTune tenant and share metrics? Prioritize logs around 07:45–08:30 PST.
2) Laura/Karthik — prepare a safe short-term mitigation plan we can roll in <30m: options include per-tenant disabling of continuous batching, reduce per-tenant max_batch_size, and/or temporarily route AstraTune to the green model variant (redwood-v2-13b-quant-stable) that uses a different caching profile.
3) Sofia/Ben — do we want to propose immediate burst capacity (Dedicated burst) while engineering fixes config? That would buy time but requires quick commercial approval.

I’ve attached the customer logs Sofia sent.

-Marissa
Engineering Manager, Accounts
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: ACTION: AstraTune hot-lane / KV config mitigation (canary plan)

Quick updates after 10m triage:
- Confirmed: hot-lane queueing spike + high KV eviction rate coincident with AstraTune morning window (07:50–08:10 PST). Eviction spikes line up with large-volume batch arrivals.
- Root cause (working hypothesis): large batch sizes + continuous batching for this tenant cause cache churn; when a head request misses, it blocks the lane and subsequent batches accumulate — classic HOL blocking.

Immediate mitigation steps (will execute now):
1) Canary change (AstraTune only):
   - Disable continuous batching for tenant (safe toggle, instant rollback).
   - Set per-tenant max_batch_size from 128 -> 32 for 2x test nodes.
   - Temporarily switch routing for 10% of traffic to redwood-v2-13b-quant-stable (no quantization micro-optimizations that interact with KV layout).
2) Cache tuning:
   - Apply a short TTL-based soft-protection rule for prefix entries for AstraTune (increase min-residency to 30s) to reduce eviction churn.
3) Observability:
   - Add a dashboard for per-tenant eviction_rate, hotlane_queue_depth, per-node batch latency.

Rollout plan: canary -> 10m observe -> expand to 50% -> full. Fallback = toggle continuous batching back on + revert max_batch_size.

I’ll post metric snapshots in 5m.
-Jonas
SRE Lead
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
